title: Humanity's Last Choice: A Common Evaluation Standard for Generative Engine Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2610.23541v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humanity's Last Choice describes the idea that the last choice people need to make is which AI system they entrust with the decisions that follow. These systems rely on external sources that content providers can edit through generative engine optimization (GEO) to increase source visibility and influence recommendations. Choosing among these systems therefore requires comparable evidence of how well they carry out user requests when exposed to GEO. Benchmarks have made progress in standardizing tasks, models, and metrics, but they often define their own spaces of GEO strategies and use different editing constraints. These differences can conflate gains from better optimization algorithms with those from greater freedom to edit sources, while making evaluation coverage difficult to compare across benchmarks. translated_title: 人类的最后抉择：生成式引擎优化的统一评估标准
translated_abstract: “人类的最后抉择”描述了这样一种理念：人们需要做出的最后一个选择，就是将后续决策托付给哪一个AI系统。这些系统依赖外部信息源，而内容提供者可以通过生成式引擎优化来编辑这些信息源，以提升信息源的可见度并影响推荐结果。因此，在这些系统之间进行选择时，需要可比较的证据，以衡量它们在受到GEO影响时执行用户请求的能力。现有基准测试在标准化任务、模型和指标方面已取得进展，但它们通常各自定义GEO策略空间，并使用不同的编辑约束。这些差异可能将更优优化算法带来的收益与更大信息源编辑自由度带来的收益混为一谈，同时使不同基准测试之间的评估覆盖范围难以比较。因此，我们呼吁建立统一的评估标准，并提出一个元分类法来描述信息源在哪里被编辑、如何被编辑（摘要原文在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文呼吁建立生成式引擎优化的统一评估标准，并提出一个元分类法来区分“优化算法改进”与“信息源编辑自由度”所带来的不同收益，从而实现对不同基准测试评估结果的公平比较。
en_tdlr: This paper calls for a common evaluation standard for generative engine optimization (GEO) and proposes a meta-taxonomy that disentangles gains from better optimization algorithms versus greater freedom in editing sources, enabling fair comparison across benchmarks.
